requirements.evidence: The two pages, routes, lang keys, navbar links and members tabs are present (routes/web.php:59-60; lang/en/ui.php:89-130; resources/views/layouts/default-page.blade.php:45-52; resources/views/livewire/entity/members.blade.php:6-21), and client ids are re-resolved through the entity (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:100-102, 207-208; app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:57-61, 101-104). But rename passes the raw name as the slug (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:147), not a re-derived slug, so the rename requirement and its multi-word edge case are not met.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes all go through the existing actions (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:135, 143-148, 210, 218; app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:74-78), user input uses #[Validate] (Queues.php:25, 43; Serve.php:30), authorization uses policies, docs and CHANGELOG are updated (docs/architecture.md:130-142; CHANGELOG.md:21), and the Bulma/sibling style is followed. Deviations: role/access logic is in the Blade view (resources/views/livewire/entity/queues.blade.php:155-157) and Members::$activeTab has no validation (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:32).

security.evidence: Every client id is resolved with entity scoping and authorized before use (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:100-102, 136-138, 207-208; app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:57-61, 101-104), output is escaped with {{ }}, lastCalledTicketId is #[Locked] (Serve.php:36-37), and callNext is rate-limited per user/entity (Serve.php:65-89). The only gap is that grantAccess/revokeAccess rely entirely on SetQueueAccess for authorization (Queues.php:205-219) and are not covered by an unauthorized test.

tests.evidence: The new tests cover the route/403, create/rename/access flows and foreign-id tampering (tests/Feature/Entity/QueuesPageTest.php:25-258), the serve selector/waiting list/modes, call errors, 403 and rate limiting (tests/Feature/Entity/ServePageTest.php:28-258), and the members tabs (tests/Feature/Entity/MembersTabsTest.php:14-55). They miss per-action unauthorized tests for the queues actions, a tamper test for the locked lastCalledTicketId, and a multi-word rename; the rename test's single-word name is why the slug defect is not caught.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses the four domain actions and existing x-label/x-input/Bulma patterns without new layers or dependencies (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:135, 143-148, 210, 218; app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:74-78). The four raw modal blocks repeat a lot of markup (resources/views/livewire/entity/queues.blade.php:40-189) and the role check in Blade (155-157) is avoidable duplication.

readability.evidence: Methods are short and clearly named, and nested state is reset centrally (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:105, 111; app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:49-93). The @php role block (queues.blade.php:155-158) and the tab markup with dangling aria-controls and href='#' (members.blade.php:9-16) make the views harder to follow.

scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves the task: two routes/components/views, members tabs, navbar, both lang files, docs and tests (routes/web.php:59-60; layouts/default-page.blade.php:45-52; docs/architecture.md:130-142; CHANGELOG.md:21; tests/Feature/Entity/*). No unrelated refactors or features were added.

issues.explanation: rename() passes 'slug: $this->renameName', i.e. the raw name, instead of a slug derived from it (Str::slug); a multi-word rename such as 'Atendimento Geral' will only work if UpdateQueue slugifies the argument internally, while the task explicitly requires the component to pass the re-derived slug. The rename test only uses the one-word 'New', so it does not catch this.

The suite has no unauthorized-call tests for create, rename, toggleActive, openAccess, grantAccess or revokeAccess, and no tamper test for the #[Locked] lastCalledTicketId; the conventions require an unauthorized and a tamper test for each Livewire action, and the only 403 covered is the route/component mount.

The tabs declare aria-controls='members-panel' and aria-controls='invites-panel', but no element with those ids (or role='tabpanel') exists in the view, so the tab semantics are broken; the anchors also use href='#' and will jump to the top. Add ids/roles/aria-labelledby to the panels or drop the dangling attributes.

Role/access logic is computed inside the Blade view with a hard-coded App\Models\UserRole::Owner/Admin check; this duplicates policy knowledge in the template (and the namespace differs from the App\Enums\* enums used elsewhere in the change), so it should move to a model/policy helper or a can('call', $accessQueue) check.

grantAccess() and revokeAccess() are public endpoints but do not call $this->authorize('manageAccess', $queue) themselves; they rely entirely on SetQueueAccess doing it. That matches the actions-own-authorization convention, but the missing component-level check plus the missing unauthorized test is a defense-in-depth gap if the action ever changes.

activeTab is a plain public property with no #[Validate]; the allow-list only lives in setActiveTab(), so a client can set the property directly to an arbitrary value and hide both panels. Add #[Validate('in:members,invites')] to enforce the contract on every write.
The view tests assert text and status but never the required aria-labels (create, row, rename, toggle, access, call-next), even though the conventions ask feature tests to assert accessible labels.

review.summary: The change adds the Queues and Serve pages, their routes, navbar links, lang keys, tests and members tabs, and it resolves every client id through the current entity. It is close, but rename does not derive the slug from the new name (and the test only uses a one-word name), several queue endpoints lack the required unauthorized tests, and the tab/modal accessibility has small defects, so it needs changes before merging. The core flows are otherwise implemented and largely follow the project conventions.
